Let $F$ be a field, let $n\in\mathbb N$ (including $0$), and let $A\in M_{n\times n}(F)$ satisfy
$A_{ij}=A_{ji}$ for every $i,j<n$ (that is, $A$ is symmetric). Its
**structural graph** is
the simple undirected graph $G_0=(V,E_0)$ with vertex set
$V=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and edge set

$$E_0:=\bigl\{\{i,j\}:0\le i<j<n,\ A_{ij}\ne0\bigr\}.$$

An **elimination ordering** is a listing $v_0,\ldots,v_{n-1}$ in which every
vertex of $V$ occurs exactly once. Define the current vertex set by
$V_k=\{v_\ell:k\le\ell<n\}$, starting with the structural graph $G_0$. At
step $k$, the **later neighbors** of $v_k$ are

$$N_k(v_k):=\{u\in V_k\setminus\{v_k\}:\{u,v_k\}\in E_k\}.$$

The filled graph $G_{k+1}=(V_{k+1},E_{k+1})$ is obtained by deleting $v_k$ and
its incident edges, retaining all edges between remaining vertices, and adding
every edge between two distinct vertices of $N_k(v_k)$. An edge added at step
$k$ that was not already in $E_k$ is a **fill edge**. Repeating this rule
defines the symbolic elimination pattern for the ordering; it is defined from
the initial graph and ordering alone, without numerical pivot values.

If $N_k(v_k)$ is nonempty, the **parent** of $v_k$ is the later neighbor
$v_\ell$ with least position $\ell>k$ in the ordering. If $N_k(v_k)$ is
empty, $v_k$ is a root. Each non-root has a unique parent, and positions strictly increase along parent edges, so there is no directed cycle. If the underlying undirected graph had a cycle, its least-position vertex would be a child of both adjacent later vertices, contradicting uniqueness. Thus the parent relation is an elimination forest.

Treat an unstored active entry as zero. operations.before: Order a rectangular coordinate subbox recursively as follows. For each coordinate whose side length is at least $2$, choose its lower median coordinate, namely the coordinate with $\lfloor(m-1)/2\rfloor$ positions below it in a side of length $m$. Let $S$ be the union of the coordinate hyperplanes at those selected medians. Delete $S$, obtaining at most $2^d$ nonempty rectangular child boxes. Recursively order the child boxes in lexicographic order of their lower corners, then append the vertices of $S$ in lexicographic order. If no coordinate has side length at least $2$, append the remaining vertex as a terminal separator. Apply this rule first to the whole grid. The resulting order is the **coordinate nested-dissection ordering**.
